App

app.Rmd
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(inspectdf)
library(ttdviewer)

App structure

The call tree below is built with stackcallr. call_tree_dir() parses the files in R/ without running them, and modules_only = TRUE keeps only the functions that call NS() or moduleServer():

stackcallr::call_tree_dir("../R", root = "launch", modules_only = TRUE)
█─launch
├─mod_input_ui
├─mod_download_ui
├─mod_summary_ui
├─mod_plot_ui
├─mod_list_ui
├─mod_input_server
├─mod_download_server
├─mod_summary_server
├─mod_list_server
└─mod_plot_server

Variable inputs

The dataset title input (input$ds_title) is collected in the mod_input_ui() and mod_input_server() functions and passed to the load_tt_data() function:

tryCatch({
    result <- load_tt_data(input$dataset_title)
    if (length(result) == 0) {
      logr_msg("Empty dataset returned", level = "WARN")
      showNotification("No data available for selected dataset",
        type = "warning", duration = 5
      )
    } else {
      logr_msg("Dataset successfully loaded in reactive",
        level = "SUCCESS"
      )
    }
    return(result)
  },
  error = function(e) {
    logr_msg(paste("Error in data reactive:", e$message),
      level = "ERROR"
    )
    showNotification(paste("Error loading data:", e$message),
      type = "error", duration = 10
    )
    return(list())
  }
)

mod_input_server() returns a list with two reactives: the dataset list (data) and the title (ds_title).

return(
    list(
      data = data,
      'ds_title' = reactive(input$ds_title)
    )
  )

In the app_server(), the inputs are assigned to the title_input and separated into selected_data and dataset_title:

# initialize modules
title_input <- mod_input_server("input")
# return the data and title
selected_data <- title_input$data
dataset_title <- title_input$ds_title

These reactive values are passed to the output modules.

List

mod_list is a simple module that collects the list of #TidyTuesday datasets from the mod_input_server():

Input Controls 

# collect data
mod_list_server(id = "listviewerlite", data = selected_data)

List Display

The list display comes from the listviewerlite package. The mod_list_server() accepts the selected_data as data()

# render data()
output$list <- renderUI({
  req(data())
  listviewerlite::listview(data())
})

Graphs

The graphs are controlled by the mod_plot module, which handles the interactive data visualizations for the #TidyTuesday dataset list. The module is designed with a flexible interface for exploring different types of plots across multiple datasets with:

  1. Unique namespace IDs and reactive data handling for flexible input processing
  2. Dynamic UI generation and event-driven updates for creating outputs based on the underlying data

Input Controls

The UI creates two main input controls:

selectInput(
  ns("dataset"),
  "Choose dataset:",
  choices = NULL,
  selected = NULL
)

This dropdown allows users to select which dataset they want to visualize. The choices are populated dynamically based on the available datasets.

checkboxGroupInput(
  ns("plots"),
  "Select plot type:",
  choices = plot_labels(),
  selected = c("types","mem","na")
)

plot_labels() maps readable names to the plot codes inspect_plot() expects; the same names are used for the plot headings:

Label Code
Column types "types"
Memory usage "mem"
Missing values "na"
Correlations "cor"
Most common values "imb"
Numeric distributions "num"
Categorical levels "cat"

The checkbox group lets users select multiple plot types simultaneously. The default selection includes three fundamental plots: column types, memory usage, and missing values analysis.

uiOutput(ns("plots_ui"))

This uiOutput() holds the plots. The server fills it based on the user’s selections.

ttd_r <- if (is.reactive(ttd)) {
  logr_msg(message = "ttd is reactive", level = "DEBUG")
  ttd
} else {
  logr_msg(
    message = "ttd is static; wrapping in reactive()", 
    level = "DEBUG")
  reactive(ttd)
}

The server function accepts reactive or static data. Reactive data comes from the input module; static data is wrapped in reactive(), so the module works either way. The observer extracts dataset names from the reactive data (ttd_r()), and provides fallback logic if names are missing (by using indices).

observe({
  tryCatch({
    ds <- names(ttd_r())
    if (is.null(ds) || length(ds) == 0) {
      ds <- seq_along(ttd_r()) %>% as.character()
      logr_msg(message = "No names in ttd; using indices", level = "WARN")
    }
    updateSelectInput(
      session, "dataset",
      choices  = ds,
      selected = ds[[1]]
    )
  }, error = function(err) {
    logr_msg(
      message = sprintf("Error populating dataset selector: %s", err$message), 
      level = "ERROR")
  })
}) |>
  bindEvent(ttd_r(), once = FALSE)

Populating the dataset selector

The selectInput() is updated with available choices and selects the first dataset by default. The bindEvent(ttd_r(), once = FALSE) ensures this runs whenever the data changes, but not on every reactive cycle.

renderUI creates plot containers dynamically by validating the input with req(), then mapping over the selected plot types with purrr::map(). The namespace function (NS()) creates a unique plot id, which also creates a unique plot container with headers and specified dimensions.

output$plots_ui <- renderUI({
  tryCatch({
    req(input$dataset, input$plots)
    purrr::map(input$plots, function(plt) {
      plot_id <- ns(paste0("plt_", plt))
      tagList(
        h4(plt),
        plotOutput(plot_id, height = "300px")
      )
    })
  }, error = function(err) {
    tagList(p(style = "color:red;", "Failed to generate plot UI."))
  })
})

Plot Display

The most complex part of the mod_plot handles the plot generation. The observer validates the dataset selection exists in the reactive list (ttd_r()), then extracts the selected dataset as a standalone data frame (df).

purrr::walk() iterates over each selected plot type and creates individual plot outputs with unique IDs using the inspect_plot() function. bindEvent() limits unnecessary updates with event-driven reactivity and responding to changes in either dataset or plot selections.

observe({
  tryCatch({
    ds_list <- req(ttd_r())
    sel_ds  <- input$dataset
    req(sel_ds %in% names(ds_list))
    df <- ds_list[[sel_ds]]
    
    purrr::walk(input$plots, function(plt) {
      out_id <- paste0("plt_", plt)
      output[[out_id]] <- renderPlot({
        tryCatch({
          inspect_plot(
            ttd = setNames(list(df), sel_ds),
            plots = plt
          )
        }, error = function(err2) {
          plot.new()
          text(0.5, 0.5, "Error generating plot", cex = 1.2, col = "red")
        })
      })
    })
  }, error = function(err) {
    logr_msg(
      message = sprintf("Error in plot observer: %s", err$message), 
      level = "ERROR")
  })
}) |>
  bindEvent(list(input$dataset, input$plots), ignoreNULL = TRUE)

inspect_plot()

The module interfaces use the inspect_plot() utility function, which uses the inspectdf package to generate different types of exploratory plots:

  • “types”: Column type distributions
  • “mem”: Memory usage analysis
  • “na”: Missing value patterns
  • “cor”: Correlation analysis
  • “imb”: Feature imbalance for categorical data
  • “num”: Numeric column summaries
  • “cat”: Categorical column summaries

The inspect_plot() function handles the complexity of determining appropriate visualizations based on data characteristics and the number of datasets.

In the main app, the module is integrated as:

# In app_ui()
bslib::nav_panel("Graphs", mod_plot_ui("viz"))

# In app_server()  
title_input <- mod_input_server("input")
selected_data <- title_input$data
mod_plot_server("viz", ttd = selected_data)

Reactive or static data

The module receives data through the ttd parameter, but it can be a reactive expression from another module or static data passed directly. selected_data is a reactive containing #TidyTuesday datasets from the mod_input module, providing a complete visualization interface within the “Graphs” tab.

The input handling also makes the module highly reusable across different contexts.

Error Handling

The module implements comprehensive error handling at multiple levels. Input validation is handled using req() to avoid processing invalid states. tryCatch() is used for graceful degradation with fallback UI elements. The logr_msg() function prints plot-level error handling at different severity levels with visual placeholders and user-friendly error messages.

Summary

The Summary tab (mod_summary_ui() and mod_summary_server()) lists each file with its rows and columns. For the file picked in its dropdown, it shows three reactable tables:

  • Summary statistics: rows, columns, missing values, complete rows, and data types, from tt_file_summary().
  • Variable information: one row per column with its type, missing count, missing percent, and unique values, from tt_var_info(). Missing percents over 10 are shaded yellow; over 50, red.
  • Data: the file itself in a searchable, sortable, paged table. Only the first 1,000 rows are shown to keep the browser responsive; the sidebar download has the full file.

Download

The sidebar download (mod_download_ui() and mod_download_server()) saves the loaded data. The first dropdown picks “All files” or one file from the title (the server fills it with names(data()) each time a title loads); the second picks the format:

Format What is written
CSV each data frame written with vroom::vroom_write()
Parquet each data frame written with nanoparquet::write_parquet()

One file downloads under its own name with the format’s extension (for example, sets.parquet). “All files” from a title with several files downloads one .zip named after the title and format (for example, lego_database_csv.zip). The internal helpers tt_download_filename() and write_tt_download() pick the name and write the file:

ttd <- load_tt_data("Space Launches")
ttdviewer:::tt_download_filename(ttd, "parquet", "Space Launches")
ttdviewer:::write_tt_download(ttd, "parquet", file = "space_launches_parquet.zip")
